hypothesis: The parent's density relaxation is gated only on *global* overflow, but the TNS cost comes from cells being pushed into *locally* congested bins; making the HPWL-driven density relaxation conditional on the *worst-region* density (not just aggregate overflow) — i.e. relax the density weight only when both total overflow is non-increasing AND the maximum per-bin density is not growing — keeps density pressure where it is actually needed without starving wirelength globally.
expected_effect: WNS slightly better or neutral, TNS better (fewer congestion-driven detours in hot regions), overflow flat-to-lower, runtime unchanged.
analysis: The hypothesis held: gating density relaxation on worst-region density improved all three cases (total +0.270, robust +0.057, all valid). Gains concentrate in TNS (bp-ng45 +11.4%, bp_fe-ng45 +13.7%) with WNS also up, consistent with the mechanism—retaining density pressure in locally congested bins stops cells being displaced into already-tight regions, reducing the TNS-driving pushes without globally starving wirelength. ariane133-ng45 moved least (+0.044), plausibly because its overflow (~117) is already high, leaving less headroom. Next step: sweep the worst-region density growth threshold (e.g., allow small positive growth vs. strict non-growth) to test sensitivity and confirm the effect isn't threshold-specific.
